I have been farming these 600 mu in Quzhou for 20 years now. I finished middle school and came straight back to the farm. I run wheat-maize double cropping on 300 mu, and the other 300 mu I split between 150 mu cotton and 150 mu stevia under contract with a company in town. With only three of us at home, I hire tractors for tillage and bring in workers for picking and harvest — you cannot manage 600 mu with family labor alone.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary tilled before planting and used Luyuan 502 improved seed, about 25 jin per mu. For fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer as base in the fall, and now at green-up I will top-dress urea. Total nitrogen for the wheat is 16 kg per mu — that is about one and a half bags of urea split between base and topdressing. I also put 7 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium per mu, all through the compound fertilizer base. I irrigate four times: we already did winter irrigation, and now I will water at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray pesticide three times — herbicide once, then insecticide and fungicide. Last year my wheat made 480 kg per mu; this year I expect 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June. I use a no-tillage planter — it is fast and the wheat stubble keeps moisture in the ground. The seed dealer told me this hybrid is selling well, and my neighbor Li used it last year and got a good harvest. I apply 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Compound fertilizer at planting, then urea top-dress at big trumpet stage. Three irrigations — seedling, big trumpet, and grain filling. Three pesticide sprays. I expect 600 kg per mu.

Cotton is on 150 mu. I rotary till in April and plant hybrid seed. Cotton needs more fertilizer than grain crops, especially potassium. I use 20 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. Four irrigations, and I spray pesticide six times because bollworms and aphids never stop on cotton. I hire 15 to 20 workers for picking in autumn. Expected yield is 275 kg seed cotton per mu.

Stevia I grow on 150 mu under contract. I rotary till and transplant in May. Stevia has shallow roots, so I irrigate five times through the season. I apply 10 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Four pesticide sprays. Expected yield is 200 kg dry leaves per mu.

I do not cut fertilizer to save money. Three years ago my cousin reduced nitrogen by half a bag per mu and his wheat yield dropped by nearly 100 kg. Losing yield is much worse than spending on inputs. But I also calculate every bag — at 600 mu, buying too much fertilizer is also real money. I find the balance by doing what worked last year and adjusting a little if the dealer or my neighbors see something new that actually works on their fields.
